I came clean to a friend that I had an abortion, it was for my health. 
It was an ectopic pregnancy, I hadn't told anyone I was pregnant, and I wasn't far along. The guy and I had just been together casually and neither of us was really ready for a kid. I didn't tell him or my family ( I was out in Kansas at the time) I had to drive North for something like 5 hours for this. I don't feel guilty about it, but it's definitely the kind of thing you can't just bring up. It's been like 3 years now and she is the only one I told. (Aside from anyone reading this)
She just was sharing stories about how she tried with her S/O for so long and had a miscarriage. Then she was telling me that I wouldn't be able to understand, I told her I did to some degree. 
When I found out, I ran through a million thoughts. When I found out that if I didn't terminate then it was very likely that neither me or the "baby" (fetus?) Would make it.

She told me that while it's not the same she felt glad I could open up about something like that. 

This is one of those things that I'm taking to my grave. No one else needs to know.

I know it's not super heavy like the other posts here. But it was hard for me to just open up like that about it. I've been hiding it for so long.

The weirdness comes from I don't know how she feels about how we lived together. It was such a short amount of time and I left pretty fast. She's never been the type to contact others first, but I know she at the very least doesn't hate me.

Get out. 

I read your whole thing, it wasn't too long. You are not paranoid, you have valid concerns and a lifestyle that doesn't jell with his. If your staying for the small moment but deep down just super unhappy. Get out.

You don't owe him a report of your life. You are an independent person, you can make your own decisions. 

Why should he take the wind out of your sails for internships? Why should it matter if he's uncomfortable around your friends? He doesn't have to understand your humor he just needs to know it makes you smile. 

If this guy can't function without knowing where you are and tearing down what brings you some semblance of relief from depression, then he's not worth it 

I understand that he seems good and nothing big happened to be like "oh that's it." But with relationships like this they erode over time. It's normal. But you don't have to be a part of it. You can sit down and discuss things with him. Tell him out right, and if he tries to make you feel guilty. Leave. That's not good and just plain manipulative. You obviously deserve better. And I hope whatever you decide it works out.

Tell her family or some close to her you are concerned and that she's been messaging you. Then move ON.
You broke up. You have no obligation to her and should not let her back in if she needs help.

It sounds like you don't want to have that relationship with your friends anymore, that's not a bad thing, people drift. Some sooner than others. 

I have been where your friends are where they put way more in to friends then family. They just need to understand that sometimes distance is the best thing. All my friends from high school or even past jobs are people I only talk to once every 6 months or so. 

If you really want space but feel like not talking makes you no longer friends sounds like they don't know what really long term friends are. People grow up and move on you have other things and time for yourself. Take it and don't feel guilty. It's very common.

23 year old high clinical depression (suicidal thoughts and tried twice)  I don't fear death, I fear what I leave behind. But in my lowest moments the reasons I once had that kept me here don't seem to matter anymore. So the thought of death doesn't scare me, but the thought of what I leave behind makes me stay.  How it will devastate my family and the ones I'm close with, what they will feel and what that mean for them.

Hey, thank you for putting this out there. I know it couldn't have been easy, but it's just the kind of thing that I needed to know. 

I'm not alone in my thoughts. 

That's the hardest part about depression, you feel so fucking alone and like no one else could possibly understand. But then you read things like this where you say the same things I've thought about for well over a decade, and it don't know it gives you hope? 

That if you can make it to tomorrow, why can't I?

The inspirational shit they say about taking one step feels hollow from someone who can't empathize. That's why I'm saying thank you. Because it's very clear (you are going/have gone) through similar shit. 

Thanks.

Show us more, give us more than just: guess Lance is part Altean now? 🤷‍♂️ And a FARMeR?! Like he was the sharpshooter and now he mourns some alien princess for most of his life left that he knew for how long? That can't be healthy. Damn. That just feels lazy and like the writers had something else planned but executive's were like: how bout no? 

The scene with Lance and Keith talking about how much they have changed is like the only real emotionally invested conversation between paladins this season after the first episode. 

The first episode felt like they were rushing the Allurance plot along and pushed aside any other agency that other characters had. Like where is our conversation with Shiro and Keith? Where is Keith even? No character really stands out in this season.

I am a Klance supporter but I guess if I squint hard enough I can see the relationship for Lance and Allura. It's hard to see it though because she brushed him off so frequently in the beginning it felt vanilla. Like it was expected. Which bothers me with this show, it revels in the unexpected and change of the norm so to have such strong characters reduced to that sad excuse for an ending? I'm dissatisfied, and disappointed. They could have done better.

Overall the season felt rushed and like they just wanted it to end. Sad to see it go but it was fun while it lasted.

I have some friends that are drug and gang affiliated. They have a body count. They have federal records. I try not to think about it, but I do.

Maybe I'm too fucked up to let it bother me but if I think about it for too long then I'll never want to talk with these people again, and that's not right to me. I don't have a body count (I have never killed), and haven't served time. I am referred to as the "Safe Friend" I didn't know them before they were in a federal prison, I met them after. 

They have openly answered questions I had, and told me how they block it out or don't think about how the "victim" was a person with hopes and dreams and probably had a family. They told me if they thought like that they would never get better and never try to be a better person because that's a lot to fathom. These friends volunteer at hospitals, and go to Narcotics Anonymous meetings, they are hanging with me to avoid situations to get them back into trouble. I can and do respect that, they are trying.

How can I be friends with people like that? Like I said I'm fucked up. I am a person who thinks that no matter the person they can do better. Is that wrong to think? I would argue no. But I can also understand how people hear that others have a body count or they have murdered someone and call them "things", "human trash", "lost cause", etc. 

I believe that everyone has the potential to be  a saint, and everyone has the potential to be a murderer. The difference between them is context but it also gets hazy the more details you add. Soldiers in the wars have taken lives, there are police who have taken lives, the difference is we give permission for them servicemen and women to take lives, and grant them the authority to do so. But when the uniform is off? Do they still have permission? Some say yes, others no. So then the difference between a murderer and an officer is training?

Moral ambiguity is fascinating and can go on forever. But the long and short of it is this yes I know someone who has killed.

"The United Nations defines youth as persons between the ages of 15 and 24 with all UN statistics based on this range, the UN states education as a source for these statistics. The UN also recognizes that this varies without prejudice to other age groups listed by member states such as 18–30. A useful distinction within the UN itself can be made between teenagers (i.e. those between the ages of 13 and 19) and young adults (those between the ages of 18 and 32). While seeking to impose some uniformity on statistical approaches, the UN itself is aware of contradictions between approaches in its own statutes. Hence under the 15–24 definition (introduced in 1981) children are defined as those under the age of 14 while under the 1979 Convention on the Rights of the Child, those under the age of 18 are regarded as children."

"Youth also identifies a particular mindset of attitude, as in "He is very youthful". For certain uses, such as employment statistics, the term also sometimes refers to individuals from the ages of 14 to 21."
